parts.title: Prologue: the seven days of creation
parts.summary: Before the first heading, God creates the heavens and the earth by his word, makes humanity male and female in his image, calls everything very good, and rests on the seventh day, which he blesses.

parts.title: The account of the heavens and the earth
parts.summary: The first heading (2:4) tells what came of the created world: the man and woman in Eden, the command and the fall, exile east of Eden, Cain's murder of Abel, the spread of Cain's line, and the birth of Seth, when people begin to call on the name of the LORD.

parts.title: The book of the generations of Adam
parts.summary: Opening with ‘the book of the generations of Adam’ (5:1), a ten-generation genealogy runs from Adam to Noah with its refrain ‘and then he died’, broken by Enoch, who walked with God. It closes with the sons of God and human violence, the LORD's grief, and Noah finding favor.

parts.title: The account of Noah
parts.summary: Noah, righteous and blameless, builds the ark; the flood undoes creation and God remembers Noah. Afterward God makes a covenant with Noah and every living creature, sets the rainbow as its sign, and grounds the value of human life in the image of God, and Noah's drunkenness exposes Ham.

parts.title: The account of Noah's sons
parts.summary: The Table of Nations (10:1) lists seventy peoples descended from Shem, Ham, and Japheth, spread across the known world. The story of Babel (11:1-9) then tells how humanity, united in language, tried to make a name for itself and was scattered.

parts.title: The account of Shem
parts.summary: A second ten-generation genealogy (11:10) narrows from Shem to Terah and his three sons, Abram, Nahor, and Haran, carrying the line of blessing through the scattered nations toward Abraham.

parts.title: The account of Terah: Abraham
parts.summary: Under Terah's heading (11:27) comes the story of his son Abram: the call and the promise of land, offspring, and blessing for all nations; covenant, circumcision, and a new name; the long wait for Isaac; the binding of Isaac; and Abraham's burial in the one piece of land he owned.

parts.title: The account of Ishmael
parts.summary: A short record (25:12) of Ishmael's twelve sons shows God keeping his promise to make Hagar's son a great nation, before the story returns to the chosen line.

parts.title: The account of Isaac: Jacob
parts.summary: Under Isaac's heading (25:19) comes the story of his twin sons. Jacob takes Esau's birthright and blessing, flees to Harran, builds a family of twelve sons amid rivalry, wrestles with God and is renamed Israel, returns to the land, and buries his father.

parts.title: The account of Esau
parts.summary: Esau's line becomes the nation of Edom. The heading appears twice (36:1 and 36:9, the second locating Esau in the hill country of Seir), and the chapter lists Edom's chiefs and its kings who reigned before any king in Israel, while Jacob settles in Canaan (37:1).

parts.title: The account of Jacob: Joseph and his brothers
parts.summary: The last heading (37:2) introduces the story of Jacob's sons. Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to rule under Pharaoh, and saves the family from famine; Judah offers himself for Benjamin; the brothers are reconciled; Jacob blesses his sons; and Joseph dies trusting God to bring Israel home.

parts.title: Oppression in Egypt and the birth of Moses
parts.summary: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt, and a fearful Pharaoh enslaves them and orders their sons killed. Moses is saved from the Nile, raised by Pharaoh's daughter, and flees to Midian after killing an Egyptian. God hears Israel's cry.

parts.title: The call of Moses
parts.summary: God appears to Moses in a burning bush, reveals his name, and sends him to Pharaoh. Moses resists, Aaron is given as his spokesman, and the first demand to Pharaoh only makes the slavery worse. God renews his promise to redeem his people.

parts.title: The plagues on Egypt
parts.summary: In a series of escalating plagues, from the Nile turned to blood to three days of darkness, God shows his power over Egypt and its gods while Pharaoh repeatedly refuses to let Israel go. The death of the firstborn is announced.

parts.title: Passover, the exodus, and the sea
parts.summary: Israel keeps the first Passover, the firstborn of Egypt die, and Pharaoh drives the people out. God leads them by pillars of cloud and fire, divides the sea for Israel, and brings the waters back on Pharaoh's army. Moses and Miriam lead a song of praise.

parts.title: Through the wilderness to Sinai
parts.summary: In the desert the people grumble over water and food, and God provides sweet water, quail, manna, and water from the rock. Israel defeats Amalek, and Jethro counsels Moses to share the work of judging the people.

parts.title: The covenant at Sinai
parts.summary: At the mountain God offers Israel a covenant, speaks the Ten Commandments, and gives the laws of the Book of the Covenant. The people agree, the covenant is sealed with blood, and Israel's leaders see the God of Israel and eat in his presence.

parts.title: Instructions for the tabernacle
parts.summary: On the mountain God gives Moses the pattern for the tabernacle, its furniture, the priests' garments, and the ordination of Aaron and his sons, closing with the Sabbath as the sign of the covenant.

parts.title: The golden calf and the covenant renewed
parts.summary: While Moses is on the mountain the people worship a golden calf. Moses intercedes, God refuses to abandon them, reveals his goodness to Moses, proclaims his character, and renews the covenant.

parts.title: The tabernacle built and filled
parts.summary: The people give generously, and skilled workers build the tabernacle exactly as commanded. Moses sets it up, and the cloud covers it as the glory of the LORD fills the tent.

parts.title: The offerings
parts.summary: Five kinds of offering (burnt, grain, peace, sin or purification, and guilt or reparation), first described from the worshiper's side and then as instructions for the priests who handle them.

parts.title: The priests ordained
parts.summary: Moses ordains Aaron and his sons over seven days. On the eighth day God's glory appears and fire consumes the offering, and then Nadab and Abihu die for offering unauthorized fire.

parts.title: Clean and unclean
parts.summary: Laws on food, childbirth, skin diseases and mold, and bodily discharges, with the rites that restore an unclean person to the community and the sanctuary.

parts.title: The Day of Atonement
parts.summary: Once a year the high priest enters the Most Holy Place to cleanse the sanctuary of Israel's impurities, and a live goat carries the people's sins away into the wilderness.

parts.title: Holiness in all of life
parts.summary: The Holiness Code: blood, sexual relations, love of neighbor, penalties, the holiness of priests and offerings, the yearly feasts, the Sabbath year and Jubilee, and the covenant's blessings and curses.

parts.title: Vows and dedications
parts.summary: Rules for dedicating people, animals, houses, and fields to the LORD, for redeeming them, and for the tithe, closing the book with a note that these commands were given at Sinai.

parts.title: The camp ordered at Sinai
parts.summary: The first census, the arrangement of the tribes around the tabernacle, the duties of the Levites, laws of purity and vows, the priestly blessing, the leaders' gifts, the second Passover, and the signals for the march.

parts.title: Setting out and the first complaints
parts.summary: Israel leaves Sinai following the cloud. The people complain at Taberah and crave meat at Kibroth-hattaavah, Moses is given seventy elders to share his burden, and Miriam and Aaron challenge Moses.

parts.title: The scouts and the refusal
parts.summary: Twelve scouts explore Canaan; ten report that it cannot be taken. The people refuse to go in, Moses intercedes, and God sentences the generation to forty years in the wilderness.

parts.title: Rebellion and the priesthood confirmed
parts.summary: Laws for life in the coming land, Korah's rebellion and its judgment, Aaron's budding staff, the duties and support of priests and Levites, and the ritual of the red heifer for cleansing from contact with death.

parts.title: The road to Moab
parts.summary: Miriam dies, Moses strikes the rock and is barred from the land, Edom refuses passage, and Aaron dies. After the bronze serpent, Israel defeats Sihon and Og and reaches the plains of Moab.

parts.title: Balaam and Baal of Peor
parts.summary: King Balak of Moab hires Balaam to curse Israel, but Balaam can speak only blessing. Then Israel falls into idolatry and sexual sin with the Moabites and Midianites at Peor, and Phinehas stops the plague.

parts.title: The new generation on the plains of Moab
parts.summary: A second census counts the new generation. Laws follow for inheritance, offerings, and vows; Joshua is commissioned; Midian is punished; two and a half tribes settle east of the Jordan; and the borders, Levitical cities, and cities of refuge are set for the land ahead.

parts.title: Moses' first address: remembering the road
parts.summary: Moses reviews the forty years from Horeb to Moab, the failure at Kadesh, the victories east of the Jordan, and calls Israel to keep the law and never make an image of God.

parts.title: The heart of the covenant
parts.summary: The Ten Commandments are repeated, followed by the Shema and extended preaching on loving God alone, remembering his grace, and refusing both pride and idolatry.

parts.title: The statutes and ordinances
parts.summary: Laws for life in the land: one place of worship, the rejection of Canaanite religion, festivals, judges, kings, priests, prophets, warfare, family, and generous care for the poor, the widow, the orphan, and the foreigner.

parts.title: Blessings and curses
parts.summary: Instructions for a covenant ceremony at Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, followed by the blessings that come with obedience and the long list of curses, ending in exile, that come with rebellion.

parts.title: The covenant renewed in Moab
parts.summary: Moses renews the covenant with the new generation, foresees exile and return, promises that God will circumcise their hearts, and sets before them life and death.

parts.title: Moses' last words and death
parts.summary: Joshua is commissioned, the law is written and entrusted to the priests, Moses sings a song of witness and blesses the tribes, and he dies on Mount Nebo in sight of the land.

parts.title: Entering the land
parts.summary: God commissions Joshua, spies are sheltered by Rahab in Jericho, Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground, sets up memorial stones, and renews circumcision and Passover at Gilgal.

parts.title: Jericho and Ai
parts.summary: The walls of Jericho fall and Rahab's family is spared. Achan's theft brings defeat at Ai until the sin is exposed, after which Ai is taken and the covenant is renewed at Mount Ebal.

parts.title: The campaigns in the south and north
parts.summary: The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty, a southern coalition is defeated, northern kings under Jabin of Hazor are defeated, and a list records the kings Israel overcame.

parts.title: Dividing the land
parts.summary: The land is allotted to the tribes east and west of the Jordan, Caleb receives Hebron, the tabernacle is set up at Shiloh, and cities of refuge and Levitical towns are designated.

parts.title: Farewell and covenant
parts.summary: The eastern tribes return home after a dispute over an altar, Joshua gives a farewell charge, and Israel renews its covenant with the LORD at Shechem before Joshua's death and burial.

parts.title: An unfinished conquest
parts.summary: After Joshua's death the tribes fight for their territories with mixed success, leaving many Canaanites in the land. The angel of the LORD rebukes Israel at Bokim.

parts.title: The pattern announced
parts.summary: A new generation forgets the LORD, and the narrator sets out the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out, and deliverance that shapes the book.

parts.title: The earlier judges
parts.summary: Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, Deborah and Barak, and Gideon deliver Israel from Aram, Moab, the Philistines, Canaan, and Midian, though Gideon's story ends in an idol.

parts.title: Abimelech, Jephthah, and the minor judges
parts.summary: Abimelech seizes kingship by murder and is destroyed, and Jephthah rescues Israel from Ammon at a terrible cost. Brief notices record Tola, Jair, Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon.

parts.title: Samson
parts.summary: A child promised and set apart as a Nazirite grows into a strong, self-willed man who fights the Philistines alone and dies bringing down their temple.

parts.title: No king in Israel
parts.summary: Two appendices show the collapse of worship and morals: Micah's idol and the Danite migration, and the outrage at Gibeah followed by a civil war against Benjamin.

parts.title: Emptiness and return
parts.summary: Famine, exile in Moab, and three deaths leave Naomi without husband or sons. She returns to Bethlehem, and Ruth refuses to leave her, pledging herself to Naomi's people and God.

parts.title: Gleaning in the field of Boaz
parts.summary: Ruth gleans in the barley harvest and happens on the field of Boaz, who treats her with unusual generosity. Naomi learns that he is a kinsman-redeemer.

parts.title: The night at the threshing floor
parts.summary: At Naomi's direction Ruth goes to Boaz at night and asks him to spread his garment over her as redeemer. He agrees, but a nearer relative must be given the first right.

parts.title: Redemption at the gate and the birth of Obed
parts.summary: Boaz settles the matter before the elders, the nearer redeemer declines, and Boaz marries Ruth. Their son Obed restores Naomi, and a genealogy leads to David.

parts.title: Samuel's birth and call
parts.summary: Hannah prays for a son and gives him to the LORD at Shiloh. While Eli's sons corrupt the priesthood, the boy Samuel hears God's word and becomes a recognized prophet.

parts.title: The ark lost and returned
parts.summary: Israel is defeated by the Philistines, the ark is captured, and Eli's house falls. The ark humbles the Philistine god Dagon and returns to Israel, and Samuel leads the people in repentance and victory.

parts.title: Israel asks for a king
parts.summary: The people demand a king like the nations. Samuel warns them, then anoints Saul, who is chosen by lot, proves himself against the Ammonites, and is confirmed as king while Samuel calls the nation to faithfulness.

parts.title: Saul's reign and rejection
parts.summary: Saul wins battles but disobeys the LORD's commands, and Samuel announces that the kingdom will be given to another.

parts.title: David at Saul's court
parts.summary: David is anointed in secret, defeats Goliath, and wins the love of Jonathan and the people, while Saul's jealousy turns murderous.

parts.title: David the fugitive
parts.summary: David flees into the wilderness, gathers a band of followers, twice spares Saul's life, and finally takes refuge among the Philistines.

parts.title: The end of Saul
parts.summary: Saul consults a medium at Endor, David is kept from fighting against Israel, and Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa.

parts.title: David king over Judah
parts.summary: David mourns Saul and Jonathan and is anointed king of Judah at Hebron. A long civil war with the house of Saul ends when Abner and Ish-bosheth are murdered, killings David publicly disowns.

parts.title: The kingdom established
parts.summary: All Israel makes David king. He takes Jerusalem, brings up the ark, receives God's covenant promise of an everlasting house, defeats his enemies, and shows kindness to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth.

parts.title: David's sin and Nathan's rebuke
parts.summary: David commits adultery with Bathsheba and has Uriah killed. Nathan confronts him with a parable, David confesses, and God forgives him but announces that the sword will not depart from his house.

parts.title: Troubles in David's house
parts.summary: Amnon rapes Tamar, Absalom murders Amnon, and after years of estrangement Absalom leads a rebellion that drives David from Jerusalem. Absalom dies, David returns, and a further revolt under Sheba is put down.

parts.title: Appendix: David's reign in retrospect
parts.summary: A deliberately arranged collection: a famine and the Gibeonites, lists of David's warriors, his song of deliverance and last words, and the census and plague that end at the threshing floor of Araunah.

parts.title: Solomon secures the throne
parts.summary: David's last days, Adonijah's bid for the crown, Solomon's anointing, David's charge, and the removal of Solomon's rivals.

parts.title: The wise king
parts.summary: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon, judges between two mothers, and organizes a prosperous kingdom.

parts.title: The temple
parts.summary: Solomon gathers materials with Hiram of Tyre, builds the temple and his palace, makes its furnishings, and dedicates it with the ark, the cloud of glory, and a long prayer.

parts.title: Glory and decline
parts.summary: God's warning, Solomon's trade and fame, the visit of the Queen of Sheba, and then his foreign wives, idolatry, enemies, and death.

parts.title: The kingdom divided
parts.summary: Rehoboam's folly splits the kingdom; Jeroboam sets up golden calves; the reigns of both kingdoms are traced to the rise of Omri and Ahab.

parts.title: Elijah, Ahab, and the prophets
parts.summary: Elijah confronts Ahab and Baal worship, flees to Horeb, and calls Elisha; Ahab fights Aram, seizes Naboth's vineyard, and dies in battle as Micaiah foretold.

parts.title: Elijah's last acts and Elisha's succession
parts.summary: Elijah announces Ahaziah's death and calls down fire on the king's soldiers, then is taken up in a whirlwind, and Elisha receives his cloak and his spirit.

parts.title: The ministry of Elisha
parts.summary: Elisha's word shapes a war against Moab, provides for a widow, raises a Shunammite's son, heals Naaman, protects Israel from Aram, and announces relief for starving Samaria and Hazael's rise in Damascus.

parts.title: Jehu's purge and Joash's rescue
parts.summary: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal in Israel, while in Judah Athaliah seizes the throne and the boy Joash is hidden, crowned, and later repairs the temple.

parts.title: The last years of Israel
parts.summary: Elisha dies, the two kingdoms rise and decline, Assyria advances, and Samaria falls, followed by a long explanation of why the northern kingdom was exiled.

parts.title: Hezekiah and Manasseh
parts.summary: Hezekiah trusts the LORD and Jerusalem survives Sennacherib's siege, but his son Manasseh fills the land with idolatry and innocent blood.

parts.title: Josiah's reform and the fall of Jerusalem
parts.summary: Josiah finds the Book of the Law and purges the land, but after his death Babylon takes Jerusalem, burns the temple, and carries Judah into exile, where Jehoiachin is at last released from prison.

parts.title: All Israel in its generations
parts.summary: Genealogies from Adam through the nations to Jacob's twelve sons, with Judah and David's line first, Levi at the center, and a closing list of those who resettled Jerusalem after the exile.

parts.title: The fall of Saul
parts.summary: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa, and the Chronicler explains that he died for his unfaithfulness, so that the LORD turned the kingdom over to David.

parts.title: David made king by all Israel
parts.summary: All Israel anoints David at Hebron, he captures Jerusalem, and long lists of warriors from every tribe show the whole nation rallying to him.

parts.title: The ark comes to Jerusalem
parts.summary: A first attempt to move the ark ends in Uzzah's death; after a three-month pause the Levites carry it properly into the city with music, sacrifice, and a psalm of thanksgiving.

parts.title: God's covenant with David
parts.summary: David wants to build God a house, but God promises instead to build David a house, a dynasty whose son will reign over God's kingdom forever.

parts.title: David's wars and victories
parts.summary: David defeats the surrounding nations and brings their tribute to Jerusalem, securing the peace in which the temple can be built.

parts.title: The census and the temple site
parts.summary: David's census brings a plague on Israel, and the place where the plague stops, the threshing floor of Ornan, becomes the site of the future temple.

parts.title: Preparing for the temple and for Solomon
parts.summary: David gathers materials, charges Solomon, organizes the Levites, priests, singers, gatekeepers, and officials, leads the people in giving, blesses God in prayer, and dies after Solomon is made king.

parts.title: Solomon and the temple
parts.summary: Solomon receives wisdom, builds and furnishes the temple, brings in the ark, prays at its dedication, and is answered by fire and glory. His wealth and fame draw the queen of Sheba and the nations.

parts.title: The kingdom divides
parts.summary: Rehoboam's harsh answer splits the nation. Judah is strengthened, then abandons the law, and is humbled by Shishak of Egypt.

parts.title: Abijah, Asa, and Jehoshaphat
parts.summary: Kings who seek the LORD find help in battle and lead reforms, though Asa ends badly and Jehoshaphat makes unwise alliances with the north.

parts.title: From Jehoram to Ahaz
parts.summary: Alliance with Ahab's house brings Athaliah's usurpation, Joash's rescue and later apostasy, and a line of kings who begin well and end poorly, down to Ahaz, who shuts the temple doors.

parts.title: Hezekiah's reform
parts.summary: Hezekiah reopens and cleanses the temple, invites all Israel to Passover, and is delivered from Sennacherib of Assyria.

parts.title: Manasseh to the exile, and a decree
parts.summary: Manasseh sins greatly and repents in captivity, Josiah renews the covenant, the last kings fall, Jerusalem is burned, and Cyrus invites the exiles to go up.

parts.title: The return under Cyrus
parts.summary: Cyrus decrees that the temple be rebuilt and returns its sacred vessels. The first exiles go home, and the book lists them family by family.

parts.title: The temple rebuilt
parts.summary: The returnees set up the altar and lay the foundation, meet opposition that halts the work for years, then resume under the prophets Haggai and Zechariah and finish the temple in the sixth year of Darius, 515 BC.

parts.title: Ezra comes to Jerusalem
parts.summary: Almost sixty years later Ezra the scribe leads a second group from Babylon with a commission from Artaxerxes to teach and apply the law of God, and arrives safely with the temple's gifts.

parts.title: The crisis of the mixed marriages
parts.summary: Ezra learns that many have married women of the surrounding peoples, prays a great prayer of confession, and leads the community in a painful covenant to separate from those marriages.

parts.title: Nehemiah's burden and commission
parts.summary: In Susa Nehemiah hears of Jerusalem's ruin, prays, asks Artaxerxes for leave, and arrives in Jerusalem, where he inspects the walls by night and calls the people to build.

parts.title: The wall rebuilt against opposition
parts.summary: Families and groups rebuild the wall section by section, while Nehemiah faces mockery, threats of attack, economic injustice among the Jews themselves, and plots against his life. The wall is finished in fifty-two days, and Nehemiah turns to the city's population, using the list of the first returnees.

parts.title: The law read and the covenant renewed
parts.summary: Ezra reads the law to the assembled people, who celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles, confess their sins in a great prayer, and sign a binding agreement to keep God's commands.

parts.title: A city peopled and a wall dedicated
parts.summary: One in ten of the people move into Jerusalem, the lists of priests and Levites are recorded, and the wall is dedicated with processions and great joy.

parts.title: Nehemiah's final reforms
parts.summary: Returning after an absence, Nehemiah expels Tobiah from a temple chamber, restores support for the Levites, enforces the Sabbath, and confronts marriages outside the covenant.

parts.title: A new queen in Susa
parts.summary: Xerxes deposes Vashti after she refuses his summons, and Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by Mordecai, is chosen as queen without revealing her people. Mordecai uncovers a plot against the king, and his deed is recorded.

parts.title: Haman's decree and Mordecai's challenge
parts.summary: Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman, who obtains a decree to destroy all the Jews on a day chosen by lot. Mordecai urges Esther to go to the king, and she resolves to go, fasting and at the risk of her life.

parts.title: Banquets and the great reversal
parts.summary: Esther invites the king and Haman to two banquets. On the night between them the king cannot sleep, Mordecai is honored by Haman himself, and at the second banquet Esther exposes Haman, who is hanged on his own gallows.

parts.title: A counter-decree and the feast of Purim
parts.summary: Mordecai is given Haman's authority and issues a decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves. On the appointed day they prevail over their enemies, and Mordecai and Esther establish Purim as a yearly festival.

parts.title: The greatness of Mordecai
parts.summary: A brief epilogue records Mordecai's high rank under Xerxes and his work for the good of his people.

parts.title: Prologue: the test in heaven and on earth
parts.summary: A prose story introduces Job, the scenes in the heavenly court, the loss of his wealth, children, and health, and the arrival of his three friends.

parts.title: Job's lament
parts.summary: Job breaks a seven-day silence by cursing the day of his birth and asking why the miserable are given life.

parts.title: The first cycle of speeches
parts.summary: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar each speak, and Job answers each one; the friends urge repentance and Job protests his innocence and appeals to God.

parts.title: The second cycle
parts.summary: The friends dwell on the fate of the wicked, and Job, deserted by everyone, reaches toward a witness and a redeemer.

parts.title: The third cycle
parts.summary: Eliphaz accuses Job of specific sins, Bildad gives a short speech, Zophar does not speak, and the debate breaks down.

parts.title: A poem on wisdom
parts.summary: People can mine the earth for treasure but cannot find wisdom; God alone knows its place, and the fear of the Lord is wisdom.

parts.title: Job's final defense
parts.summary: Job remembers his former honor, laments his present shame, and swears a series of oaths of innocence, calling on God to answer.

parts.title: The speeches of Elihu
parts.summary: A younger man, angry at Job and at the friends, argues that God speaks through suffering to warn and to save.

parts.title: The LORD speaks from the whirlwind
parts.summary: God questions Job about creation and its wild creatures, and Job responds in humility and repentance.

parts.title: Epilogue
parts.summary: The LORD rebukes the friends, accepts Job's prayer for them, and restores Job's household and fortunes.

parts.title: The gateway
parts.summary: Two untitled psalms introduce the whole book: the blessed life of the one who meditates on God's instruction, and the reign of the king God has installed on Zion.

parts.title: Book 1: David's prayers
parts.summary: Almost all attributed to David, many of them laments from danger and distress, with songs of trust and praise such as Psalms 8, 19, and 23. It closes with a doxology at 41:13.

parts.title: Book 2: Korah, David, and the king
parts.summary: Psalms of the sons of Korah and of David, which prefer the general word God to the name LORD. It ends with a prayer for the king (Psalm 72) and the note that the prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.

parts.title: Book 3: The crisis
parts.summary: Mostly psalms of Asaph and Korah, full of communal lament over the ruin of the sanctuary and the nation. It ends with Psalm 89, which asks how God's covenant with David can stand when the crown lies in the dust.

parts.title: Book 4: The LORD reigns
parts.summary: Opening with a prayer of Moses, this book answers the crisis by looking back past the monarchy to God as Israel's eternal dwelling place, and by proclaiming that the LORD is king (Psalms 93 and 95 to 99).

parts.title: Book 5: Return and thanksgiving
parts.summary: Psalms of thanksgiving for rescue, the great meditation on God's word in Psalm 119, the Songs of Ascents for pilgrims, and a final group of Davidic psalms, with Psalm 110's royal priest-king near its opening.

parts.title: The final Hallelujah
parts.summary: Five psalms that each begin and end with praise the LORD, closing the book with everything that has breath praising God.

parts.title: A father's instruction and Wisdom's call
parts.summary: A prologue stating the book's purpose, then a series of longer poems in which a father urges his son toward wisdom and away from violent men and the adulterous woman, with speeches by Wisdom herself, including her place at creation in chapter 8.

parts.title: The proverbs of Solomon
parts.summary: The largest collection: several hundred mostly two-line sayings, many built on the contrast between the righteous and the wicked, the wise and the foolish, covering speech, work, wealth, family, and the king.

parts.title: The words of the wise
parts.summary: Two shorter collections of longer sayings, the first closely related to the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, with advice on the poor, rulers, drunkenness, and laziness.

parts.title: Proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men
parts.summary: A second Solomonic collection gathered in the days of King Hezekiah, rich in comparisons from nature and daily life and in counsel about kings and fools.

parts.title: The words of Agur and Lemuel
parts.summary: Agur's humble confession and his numerical sayings, followed by a queen mother's counsel to her son the king on wine, women, and justice for the poor.

parts.title: The woman of noble character
parts.summary: An acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, praising a capable woman who fears the LORD, closing the book as it began, with wisdom embodied.

parts.title: Title and opening poem
parts.summary: The narrator introduces the Teacher and his motto, and a poem pictures the endless, wearying cycles of generations, sun, wind, and rivers, where nothing is new and nothing is remembered.

parts.title: The king's experiment
parts.summary: Speaking as a king, the Teacher tests wisdom, pleasure, building, and wealth, and finds that death erases their gains, yet he ends by calling daily food and work a gift from God's hand.

parts.title: A time for everything
parts.summary: The poem of the times, followed by reflection on God's hidden work, eternity in the human heart, injustice, and the shared death of humans and beasts.

parts.title: Observations under the sun
parts.summary: Oppression, envy, loneliness, fickle politics, careful worship, the traps of wealth, and the sorrow of having goods without the power to enjoy them.

parts.title: Wisdom tested
parts.summary: Collections of sayings on what is better, on the limits of wisdom, on living under kings, and on the injustice that no one can explain.

parts.title: Life before death
parts.summary: Since the same end comes to all, the Teacher urges joy, energy, and boldness in the time given, and closes with a haunting poem on old age and death.

parts.title: Epilogue
parts.summary: The narrator repeats the motto, describes the Teacher's work, and gives the conclusion: fear God, keep his commandments, and remember that God will judge every deed.

parts.title: Title
parts.summary: The superscription names the book the Song of Songs, the finest of songs, and connects it with Solomon.

parts.title: Longing and first delight
parts.summary: The woman longs for her beloved, explains her sun-darkened skin, and the lovers trade praise until she rests in his embrace and gives the first charge not to awaken love too soon.

parts.title: The spring invitation and the night search
parts.summary: He comes leaping over the hills to call her away into the springtime; later she searches the city at night, finds him, and repeats the charge.

parts.title: The royal wedding
parts.summary: Solomon's wedding procession arrives, the man praises his bride from head to breast, calls her a locked garden, and at her invitation enters his garden.

parts.title: Absence and praise
parts.summary: She hesitates to open to him, he departs, and she searches and is beaten by the watchmen; asked what makes him special, she praises him from head to foot, and they are reunited.

parts.title: Admiration and invitation
parts.summary: He praises her again as unique among all women, and she invites him to the countryside and longs to love him openly.

parts.title: Love as strong as death
parts.summary: The climax declares love stronger than death and beyond price, followed by closing scenes about a little sister, Solomon's vineyard, and a final call to the beloved.

parts.title: Judah on trial and the promised king
parts.summary: Oracles of judgment on Judah and Jerusalem, the call of Isaiah, the crisis of King Ahaz, and promises of Immanuel and a righteous king from David's line, ending in a song of praise.

parts.title: Oracles against the nations
parts.summary: Judgment on Babylon, Assyria, Philistia, Moab, Damascus, Egypt, Tyre, and others. The Lord who judges Judah rules every nation.

parts.title: Judgment and feast for the whole world
parts.summary: Often called the Isaiah apocalypse: the earth laid waste, then a banquet on Zion where God swallows up death and wipes away tears.

parts.title: Woes, false trust, and the coming kingdom
parts.summary: Warnings against trusting Egypt and against Jerusalem's leaders, alternating with visions of a righteous king and the desert blooming as the redeemed return.

parts.title: Hezekiah, Assyria, and Babylon
parts.summary: Narrative of Sennacherib's siege and Jerusalem's deliverance, Hezekiah's illness and recovery, and his display of treasure to Babylonian envoys, which points ahead to exile. These chapters close the first major part of the book, chapters 1 to 39.

parts.title: Comfort for the exiles
parts.summary: The second major part (40 to 55) begins: God comes to bring his people home, proves himself the only God against Babylon's idols, and names Cyrus as his instrument.

parts.title: The Servant and the restoration of Zion
parts.summary: The Servant is called to restore Israel and bring light to the nations, suffers and dies for the sins of many, and Zion is invited to rejoice in an everlasting covenant.

parts.title: The waiting community and the new creation
parts.summary: The third major part addresses the returned community: true worship and justice, confession of sin, the glory of a restored Zion, and new heavens and a new earth.

parts.title: The call of the prophet
parts.summary: God appoints Jeremiah as a prophet to the nations, gives him two visions (an almond branch and a boiling pot tilting from the north), and promises to stand with him against all opposition.

parts.title: Warnings and judgment on Judah
parts.summary: Poems and sermons expose Judah's unfaithfulness, attack false trust in the temple, and announce disaster from the north. Symbolic acts, the prophet's confessions, and words to the kings run through this section, which ends with the cup of God's wrath and the prediction of seventy years under Babylon.

parts.title: Conflict with priests and prophets
parts.summary: Jeremiah is put on trial for his temple sermon, wears a yoke to urge submission to Babylon, confronts the prophet Hananiah, and writes to the exiles telling them to settle in Babylon.

parts.title: The book of comfort
parts.summary: Promises of restoration: the return of the exiles, Rachel's weeping answered, the new covenant, Jeremiah's purchase of a field as a sign of the future, and the righteous branch of David.

parts.title: The last days of Jerusalem and after
parts.summary: Stories of the siege, the burned scroll, Jeremiah's imprisonment, the fall of the city, the murder of Gedaliah, and the flight to Egypt, closing with a word of assurance to Baruch.

parts.title: Oracles against the nations
parts.summary: Judgments on Egypt, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Elam, and at greatest length Babylon itself, the instrument of judgment that will in turn be judged.

parts.title: The fall of Jerusalem retold
parts.summary: A historical appendix, closely parallel to 2 Kings 24-25, recounts the city's destruction and ends with the release of King Jehoiachin in Babylon, a small light at the close of the book.

parts.title: The lonely city
parts.summary: An acrostic of twenty-two three-line stanzas. A narrator describes Jerusalem as a widow with no one to comfort her, and then the city speaks for herself, confessing her sin and begging passers-by and the LORD to look at her pain.

parts.title: The LORD as enemy
parts.summary: A second acrostic describes the destruction as the work of God's anger: the temple, walls, king, priests, and prophets all brought down. The poet weeps over starving children and urges the city to cry out to God, and the city's prayer ends in raw protest.

parts.title: The man who has seen affliction
parts.summary: A triple acrostic of sixty-six verses. One sufferer describes God's hand against him, then turns to hope in the LORD's loving devotion and faithfulness, calls the people to repent, and prays for vindication.

parts.title: Gold grown dim
parts.summary: A fourth acrostic contrasts the city's former glory with the horrors of the siege, blames prophets and priests, recalls the capture of the king, and ends with a word that Zion's punishment is complete and Edom's is coming.

parts.title: Remember us, O LORD
parts.summary: A communal prayer of twenty-two lines without the acrostic. The people describe life under foreign rule, confess their sin, affirm that God reigns forever, and ask to be restored, ending on an unresolved question.

parts.title: The call by the Kebar canal
parts.summary: Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD on a mobile throne, is commissioned as a prophet to a rebellious house, eats a scroll, and is appointed a watchman.

parts.title: Judgment on Jerusalem
parts.summary: Sign-acts and oracles announce the siege and fall of the city. In a vision the prophet sees idolatry in the temple and watches the glory of God depart. Allegories, case law on responsibility, and laments follow, ending on the day the siege begins and the prophet's wife dies.

parts.title: Oracles against the nations
parts.summary: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom, Philistia, Tyre, Sidon, and above all Egypt, nations that gloated over Judah or trusted in their own power.

parts.title: Restoration promised
parts.summary: After news of the city's fall, the prophet's mouth is opened. God promises a true shepherd, a new heart and spirit, the resurrection of the nation from dry bones, the reunion of Israel and Judah, and final victory over Gog.

parts.title: The new temple and the returning glory
parts.summary: A vision of a restored temple and land. The glory of the LORD returns from the east, a river flows from the sanctuary to bring life, and the city is named The LORD is there.

parts.title: Faithful in Babylon
parts.summary: Daniel and his three friends are taken into the king's service, refuse the royal food, and are given wisdom by God. The chapter, in Hebrew, introduces the characters and the setting of the whole book.

parts.title: The Aramaic chapters: kingdoms and the kingdom of God
parts.summary: Stories of dreams, a furnace, a humbled king, writing on a wall, and a lions' den, framed by two visions of four kingdoms (chapters 2 and 7). Chapter 7 begins the visions but belongs to this Aramaic unit.

parts.title: The ram and the goat
parts.summary: The book returns to Hebrew with a vision of Persia and Greece and a little horn that attacks the sanctuary, widely identified with Antiochus IV.

parts.title: Daniel's prayer and the seventy weeks
parts.summary: Reading Jeremiah's seventy years, Daniel confesses Israel's sin, and Gabriel answers with a prophecy of seventy weeks of years.

parts.title: The final vision
parts.summary: A long revelation of wars between the kings of the north and south, the persecution of the faithful, and the promise of resurrection at the end.

parts.title: Hosea's marriage and the LORD's marriage
parts.summary: Hosea marries Gomer, and their children's names announce judgment. The LORD indicts unfaithful Israel as a wife gone after Baal, then promises to woo her back. Hosea buys back his wife, a picture of Israel's discipline and return.

parts.title: No knowledge of God in the land
parts.summary: The LORD brings charges against Israel: faithless priests, idolatry, sexual immorality at the shrines, and rulers who run to Assyria. A call to return (6:1-3) is answered by a God who finds their loyalty as short-lived as morning mist.

parts.title: Sowing the wind
parts.summary: Kings made without God, calf images, foreign alliances, and empty festivals will bring invasion and exile. Israel's history of sin, from Baal-peor to Gibeah, will be repaid.

parts.title: The Father's love
parts.summary: God remembers calling his son out of Egypt and teaching him to walk. Though Israel will go into exile, God refuses to destroy him completely and promises a return.

parts.title: From Jacob to the final call
parts.summary: Israel's deceit is traced back to its ancestor Jacob, and its idolatry to forgetting the God of the exodus. After a final announcement of death, the book closes with an invitation to return and God's promise to heal and love freely.

parts.title: The locust plague and a call to lament
parts.summary: Successive swarms have devoured the land, cutting off food, wine, and the temple offerings. Joel summons every group to mourn and to gather for a fast, and he names the disaster as a sign of the Day of the LORD.

parts.title: The Day of the LORD and a call to return
parts.summary: An unstoppable army, led by the LORD himself, darkens the land. Yet even now the LORD calls his people to return with all their heart, and Joel summons the whole community, from infants to newlyweds, to a sacred assembly.

parts.title: The LORD answers: restoration and the Spirit
parts.summary: God takes pity, drives away the northern army, and restores rain, grain, wine, and oil. Afterward he will pour out his Spirit on all people, and everyone who calls on his name will be saved.

parts.title: Judgment of the nations and Zion's security
parts.summary: The nations that scattered, sold, and plundered God's people are summoned to the Valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment. The LORD roars from Zion, becomes a refuge for his people, and makes the land flow with abundance.

parts.title: Judgment on the nations, then on Judah and Israel
parts.summary: Eight oracles in the same pattern condemn Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab, Judah, and finally Israel, whose oppression of the poor receives the longest indictment.

parts.title: Hear this word: privilege and accountability
parts.summary: Because God chose Israel, he will hold it to account. The wealthy of Samaria, the shrines of Bethel, and a people who refused every earlier warning are summoned to meet their God.

parts.title: Lament and woe
parts.summary: A funeral song for fallen Israel, a call to seek the LORD and establish justice, a warning that the Day of the LORD will be darkness, and woes on the complacent rich.

parts.title: Five visions and a confrontation
parts.summary: Visions of locusts, fire, a plumb line, summer fruit, and the Lord at the altar announce judgment, interrupted by Amaziah the priest's order that Amos leave Bethel.

parts.title: The fallen tent of David restored
parts.summary: After judgment, God will raise up the house of David, restore his people's fortunes, and plant them in their land never again to be uprooted.

parts.title: Edom's pride will be brought down
parts.summary: A summons to battle against Edom. Its mountain security, its hidden treasures, its allies, and its wise men will all fail it.

parts.title: The charge: violence against a brother
parts.summary: Edom stood aloof, then gloated, looted, and handed over Judah's fugitives on the day Jerusalem fell.

parts.title: The Day of the LORD for all nations
parts.summary: What Edom has done will be done to it. Deliverance will come on Mount Zion, and the house of Jacob will consume the house of Esau.

parts.title: The land restored and the kingdom the LORD's
parts.summary: Returning exiles possess the land on every side, deliverers go up to Mount Zion, and the kingdom belongs to the LORD.

parts.title: Jonah runs, and the sailors fear the LORD
parts.summary: Jonah flees toward Tarshish. God sends a storm, the sailors throw Jonah into the sea, the sea grows calm, and the sailors worship the LORD. A great fish swallows Jonah.

parts.title: Jonah's prayer from the depths
parts.summary: From inside the fish Jonah prays a psalm of thanksgiving for rescue from death. The fish puts him out on dry land.

parts.title: Nineveh repents
parts.summary: Jonah preaches a five-word warning in Hebrew. The whole city, led by its king, fasts and turns from violence, and God relents.

parts.title: Jonah's anger and God's question
parts.summary: Jonah is furious at God's mercy. God uses a plant, a worm, and a hot wind to teach him, and ends with a question about his compassion for Nineveh.

parts.title: First cycle: judgment on Samaria and Judah, then a remnant gathered
parts.summary: God comes in judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem; the towns of the Shephelah mourn; land-grabbers are condemned. The cycle ends with the LORD gathering the remnant like sheep.

parts.title: Second cycle: corrupt leaders, then a coming ruler
parts.summary: Rulers, prophets, and priests are indicted and Zion's fall is announced. Then the mountain of the LORD is raised, the scattered are gathered, and a ruler comes from Bethlehem.

parts.title: Third cycle: God's lawsuit, then his unmatched mercy
parts.summary: God brings a case against his people and states what he requires. Micah laments the corruption of society, then waits for God and ends with a hymn to the God who pardons.

parts.title: The LORD, avenger and refuge
parts.summary: A hymn, partly shaped as an alphabetic acrostic, describing God's power over nature and his judgment on enemies, and his care for those who trust him.

parts.title: Judgment for Nineveh, relief for Judah
parts.summary: Oracles alternate between Nineveh's doom and Judah's release from the yoke, ending with the messenger of peace on the mountains.

parts.title: The attack on Nineveh
parts.summary: A vivid picture of the assault: red shields, flashing chariots, opened river gates, plunder, and the empty den of the Assyrian lion.

parts.title: Woe to the city of blood
parts.summary: A taunt song exposing Nineveh's violence and seduction, comparing it to fallen Thebes, and ending with its incurable wound and the world's applause.

parts.title: First complaint: how long will injustice go on?
parts.summary: Habakkuk cries out about violence and the paralysis of justice in Judah.

parts.title: God's answer: the Chaldeans are coming
parts.summary: God announces that he is raising up the ruthless Babylonians to judge Judah.

parts.title: Second complaint: why use the wicked?
parts.summary: Habakkuk asks how a pure God can let a more wicked nation swallow the more righteous, then waits on his watchtower.

parts.title: God's answer: the vision, faith, and five woes
parts.summary: God commands that the vision be written down, declares that the righteous will live by faith, and announces five woes on Babylon's greed, violence, exploitation, and idolatry.

parts.title: Habakkuk's prayer
parts.summary: A psalm recalling God's mighty coming, ending with the resolve to rejoice in God even when everything fails.

parts.title: Heading
parts.summary: The word of the LORD to Zephaniah, a descendant of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah.

parts.title: The Day of the LORD against Judah and the world
parts.summary: God announces universal judgment, focused on Jerusalem's idolatry, violence, and complacency, and describes the great day of wrath.

parts.title: Seek the LORD
parts.summary: A call to the humble of the land to seek the LORD, righteousness, and humility before the day arrives.

parts.title: Judgment on the nations
parts.summary: Oracles against Philistia, Moab and Ammon, Cush, and Assyria, with promises that Judah's remnant will possess their lands and the nations will worship the LORD.

parts.title: Woe to Jerusalem
parts.summary: The rebellious city's leaders are condemned, and God's righteous presence in her is contrasted with her refusal of correction.

parts.title: A purified people and a rejoicing God
parts.summary: God promises pure lips for the peoples, a humble remnant in Zion, and a song in which he rejoices over his people and gathers the scattered.

parts.title: First message: consider your ways
parts.summary: Haggai confronts the people for leaving God's house in ruins while they live in paneled houses, and links their failing harvests to that neglect.

parts.title: The people obey
parts.summary: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant obey and fear the LORD; God promises his presence and stirs their spirits, and work begins.

parts.title: Second message: the latter glory
parts.summary: God encourages builders who think the new temple is nothing compared with the old, promising his Spirit, the shaking of the nations, and greater glory.

parts.title: Third message: from this day I will bless
parts.summary: Through questions about ritual purity, God shows that the people's defilement has spoiled their offerings, and promises blessing from the day of the foundation onward.

parts.title: Fourth message: Zerubbabel, the signet ring
parts.summary: God promises to overthrow the kingdoms and to make Zerubbabel his chosen signet ring.

parts.title: A call to return
parts.summary: Zechariah's first message, in late 520 BC, calls the people to return to the LORD and not to repeat their fathers' refusal to listen to the prophets.

parts.title: Eight night visions and a crowning
parts.summary: In one night Zechariah sees eight visions, from the horsemen among the myrtles to the four chariots, each interpreted by an angel. They promise God's return to Jerusalem, judgment on the nations, the cleansing of the high priest and the land, and the completion of the temple, and they close with a symbolic crown and a word about the Branch.

parts.title: Fasts turned to feasts
parts.summary: A question about fasting, in 518 BC, prompts a call to justice and mercy, a reminder of why the exile came, and ten promises of a restored Jerusalem to which the nations will come seeking God.

parts.title: The first burden: the coming king and the rejected shepherd
parts.summary: God marches against Israel's neighbors, a humble king rides into Zion, the scattered people are gathered, and a prophetic shepherd is rejected and valued at thirty pieces of silver.

parts.title: The second burden: Jerusalem cleansed and the LORD as king
parts.summary: Jerusalem is besieged and rescued, the people mourn for the one they have pierced, a fountain is opened to cleanse them, the shepherd is struck, and the LORD becomes king over all the earth.

parts.title: God's love for Jacob
parts.summary: The first disputation answers the question how God has loved Israel by pointing to his choice of Jacob over Esau and the ruin of Edom.

parts.title: The priests who despise God's name
parts.summary: God indicts the priests for offering defective animals and for corrupting their calling to teach, contrasting them with the covenant faithfulness of Levi.

parts.title: Faithlessness in marriage
parts.summary: The people break faith with God and with one another by marrying worshipers of foreign gods and divorcing the wives of their youth.

parts.title: The coming messenger and the Lord's refining
parts.summary: To those who ask where the God of justice is, the LORD promises a messenger to prepare his way and his own sudden coming to refine and judge.

parts.title: Return and bring the tithe
parts.summary: God calls the people to return to him and to stop robbing him in tithes and offerings, promising blessing if they trust him.

parts.title: The day that is coming
parts.summary: To those who say serving God is futile, God promises a scroll of remembrance, a day of burning for the arrogant and healing for the faithful, and Elijah before the great day of the LORD.

parts.title: The origins of the Messiah
parts.summary: Opening with “the record of the genealogy” (1:1), literally the book of the genesis, this section answers who Jesus is and where he comes from: his descent from Abraham and David, his conception by the Spirit, the Magi and the flight to Egypt, John's preaching, the baptism, the testing in the wilderness, and the move to Capernaum.

parts.title: The kingdom announced: the Sermon on the Mount
parts.summary: Marked by “From that time on Jesus began to preach” (4:17), Jesus calls disciples and teaches the first discourse (chapters 5 to 7), which closes with the first ending formula and the crowds' astonishment at his authority (7:28-29).

parts.title: Deeds of the Messiah and the mission discourse
parts.summary: Ten miracles in chapters 8 and 9 show the authority of the one who taught on the mountain; he then sends the Twelve with the second discourse (chapter 10), which ends with the formula at 11:1.

parts.title: Rejection and the parables of the kingdom
parts.summary: John's question from prison opens a section of mounting doubt and opposition, and Jesus answers in the third discourse, the parables of chapter 13, closed by the formula at 13:53.

parts.title: Who is he?
parts.summary: Rejected at Nazareth, Jesus feeds great crowds, walks on the sea, and meets a Canaanite woman's faith, until Peter confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus speaks of building his church (16:16-18).

parts.title: The way of the cross and the life of the community
parts.summary: A second “From that time on Jesus began” (16:21) turns the story toward Jerusalem and the cross. After the transfiguration comes the fourth discourse (chapter 18), on humility, straying sheep, and forgiveness.

parts.title: To Jerusalem, and the end of the age
parts.summary: Leaving Galilee (19:1), Jesus goes up to Jerusalem, enters as king, clears the temple, and confounds his questioners. The fifth discourse, the woes of chapter 23 and the teaching on the Mount of Olives (chapters 24 and 25), speaks of the temple's fall, his coming, and the last judgment.

parts.title: Passion and resurrection
parts.summary: The last ending formula (26:1) opens the passion: the anointing, the last supper, Gethsemane, the trials, the crucifixion, and the burial, then the empty tomb and the risen Jesus sending his disciples to all nations with the promise to be with them always.

parts.title: The beginning of the gospel
parts.summary: Framed by the word gospel (1:1 and 1:14-15), the prologue tells the reader who Jesus is before any character knows: John prepares the way, Jesus is baptized and named Son by the Father's voice, is driven into the wilderness, and then announces that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God has come near.

parts.title: Authority in Galilee
parts.summary: The section opens beside the sea with the call of four fishermen (1:16-20). Jesus teaches with authority, casts out spirits, heals, and forgives sins, and a chain of five controversies (2:1-3:6) ends with Pharisees and Herodians plotting to destroy him.

parts.title: Parables, power, and rejection
parts.summary: Opening with a summary by the sea (3:7-12) and the appointment of the Twelve (3:13-19), the section sets Jesus' new family against misunderstanding relatives and hostile scribes, teaches in parables, shows authority over sea, demons, disease, and death, and closes with his rejection at Nazareth (6:1-6).

parts.title: Bread and blindness
parts.summary: Like the two before it, this section begins with the disciples, now sent out two by two (6:7-13). John is executed, Jesus feeds great crowds twice and walks on the sea, and the section ends with the disciples still failing to understand about the loaves (8:14-21) and a blind man healed in two stages (8:22-26).

parts.title: On the way to the cross
parts.summary: Mark marks this section with the phrase on the way (8:27, 9:33-34, 10:32, 10:52). Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, and on the road to Jerusalem Jesus three times predicts his death and resurrection and each time teaches what following him costs. A blind man healed at Jericho, who follows him on the way, closes the section.

parts.title: Jesus in Jerusalem
parts.summary: From the approach to the city (11:1), Mark counts the days (11:11, 11:12, 11:20). Jesus enters Jerusalem, clears the temple, debates the authorities, and on the Mount of Olives foretells the temple's destruction and the coming of the Son of Man.

parts.title: The passion
parts.summary: Opening with the note that the Passover was two days away (14:1), and then marked by hours (15:1, 15:25, 15:33-34, 15:42), the passion tells of the anointing, the last meal, Gethsemane, the betrayal, the trials, Peter's denial, the crucifixion, and the burial.

parts.title: The empty tomb
parts.summary: The women find the tomb open and hear that Jesus has risen and is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee; they flee, saying nothing to anyone, for they were afraid. Here the oldest complete manuscripts end.

parts.title: The longer ending
parts.summary: A summary of resurrection appearances, the commission, and the ascension, found in most later manuscripts and known by the late second century but absent from Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus; most modern Bibles print it with a note.

parts.title: Preface to Theophilus
parts.summary: One long, formal sentence tells how the work was made: earlier accounts, eyewitness tradition, careful investigation, and an orderly account written so that Theophilus may know the certainty of what he was taught.

parts.title: The births of John and Jesus
parts.summary: Opening “In the time of Herod king of Judea” (1:5) and written in the style of the Greek Old Testament, paired announcements, births, and songs show God keeping his promises to Israel, ending with the boy Jesus in his Father's house.

parts.title: Preparation for ministry
parts.summary: A six-part date by emperor, governor, tetrarchs, and high priests (3:1-2) opens John's preaching. Jesus is baptized and named beloved Son, his genealogy runs back to Adam, and he is tested in the wilderness.

parts.title: Ministry in Galilee
parts.summary: Marked by “Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit” (4:14), this section opens with the sermon at Nazareth and moves through healings, forgiveness, the call of disciples, and teaching, to Peter's confession and the first predictions of suffering.

parts.title: The road to Jerusalem
parts.summary: The turning point is marked in the text: “As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem” (9:51). Reminders of the destination recur (13:22, 17:11, 18:31) as Jesus teaches on discipleship, prayer, wealth, and the kingdom, with many parables found only in Luke.

parts.title: Teaching in Jerusalem
parts.summary: Marked by “He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem” (19:28), Jesus enters the city, weeps over it, clears the temple, answers his opponents, and foretells Jerusalem's destruction and the coming of the Son of Man.

parts.title: The passion
parts.summary: Jesus shares the Passover meal, prays on the Mount of Olives, is betrayed, tried before the council, Pilate, and Herod, crucified between two criminals, and buried.

parts.title: Resurrection and ascension
parts.summary: The women find the tomb empty, the risen Jesus meets disciples on the Emmaus road and in Jerusalem, opens the Scriptures to them, and is carried up into heaven, and the disciples return to the temple praising God.

parts.title: Prologue: the Word made flesh
parts.summary: A poem-like opening presents Jesus as the eternal Word, the agent of creation, the light rejected by his own and received by those who become children of God, and the one who has made the unseen Father known.

parts.title: The testimony of John and the first disciples
parts.summary: Opening with the marker “And this was John’s testimony” (1:19), a sequence of days shows the Baptist pointing to Jesus as the Lamb of God and the first disciples following him and naming him Messiah, Son of God, and King of Israel.

parts.title: From Cana to Cana
parts.summary: The Gospel numbers its first two signs, both done at Cana in Galilee (2:11, 4:54), and between them Jesus clears the temple, speaks with Nicodemus at night and a Samaritan woman at a well, and is received by Samaritans as Savior of the world.

parts.title: Signs and conflict at the feasts
parts.summary: The narrative is marked by Jewish festivals: an unnamed feast (5:1), Passover (6:4), Tabernacles (7:2), and Dedication (10:22). Jesus heals, feeds the crowds, and declares himself bread, light, and shepherd, and the section closes where the Gospel began, beyond the Jordan where John had first baptized (10:40-42).

parts.title: Lazarus raised and the hour arrives
parts.summary: The raising of Lazarus leads the council to plot Jesus' death. He is anointed at Bethany, enters Jerusalem, and announces that his hour has come (12:23). The public ministry closes with the narrator's verdict that despite so many signs many did not believe (12:37), and with Jesus' last public appeal.

parts.title: The farewell at the table
parts.summary: Marked by the words that Jesus knew his hour had come (13:1), this section gives one evening five chapters: the foot washing, the new command to love, the promise of the Holy Spirit, the vine and the branches, and Jesus' prayer for his followers.

parts.title: Arrest, cross, and resurrection
parts.summary: Jesus is arrested, tried before Annas and Pilate, crucified as King of the Jews, and buried. The risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, to the disciples, and to Thomas, and the section closes with the Gospel's own statement of its purpose (20:30-31).

parts.title: Epilogue by the sea
parts.summary: After the purpose statement, a further chapter tells of a great catch of fish in Galilee, the restoration of Peter with a threefold question of love, and the beloved disciple, whose testimony stands behind the book (21:24). Many scholars regard it as an epilogue added in the final edition; it is found in every surviving manuscript.

parts.title: Waiting and Pentecost
parts.summary: The risen Jesus commissions his apostles and ascends. Matthias replaces Judas, and the Spirit comes at Pentecost, followed by Peter's sermon and the birth of the Jerusalem church.

parts.title: Witness in Jerusalem
parts.summary: Healing, preaching, arrest, and growth in the city. The church shares its goods, faces discipline and internal tension, and appoints seven to serve. Stephen's speech and death close the Jerusalem section.

parts.title: Judea, Samaria, and the door to the nations
parts.summary: Persecution scatters the church. Philip preaches in Samaria and to an Ethiopian, Saul is converted, Peter is sent to Cornelius, a mixed church forms at Antioch, and Herod Agrippa I opposes the apostles and dies.

parts.title: The first mission and the Jerusalem council
parts.summary: Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul through Cyprus and southern Asia Minor. The church in Jerusalem decides that Gentile believers need not be circumcised.

parts.title: Paul's missions around the Aegean
parts.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece and spends about three years in Ephesus, planting churches, facing riots, and finally setting his face toward Jerusalem.

parts.title: Paul on trial and the road to Rome
parts.summary: Paul is arrested in the temple, defends himself before crowds, councils, governors, and King Agrippa II, appeals to Caesar, survives a shipwreck, and preaches in Rome under house arrest.

parts.title: Greeting and theme
parts.summary: Paul introduces himself, his gospel about God's Son, and his long-delayed plan to visit Rome, then states the letter's theme: the gospel is God's power for salvation, revealing his righteousness by faith.

parts.title: The whole world under sin
parts.summary: Gentiles who suppressed what they knew of God, and Jews who had the law and did not keep it, stand together before God's judgment. No one is declared righteous by works of the law.

parts.title: Righteousness through faith
parts.summary: God has revealed his righteousness apart from the law through faith in Jesus Christ (or, as some read the Greek, the faithfulness of Jesus Christ), whose death is the place of atonement. Abraham, counted righteous by faith before circumcision, is the father of all who believe.

parts.title: New life and sure hope
parts.summary: Justified believers have peace with God. Christ undoes Adam's ruin, believers die and rise with him, the law's role is explored, and life in the Spirit ends in the hope that nothing can separate them from God's love.

parts.title: God's faithfulness and Israel
parts.summary: Paul grieves Israel's unbelief and argues that God's word has not failed. God's mercy is free, a remnant believes, Gentiles are grafted in, and all Israel will be saved.

parts.title: The life of a people shaped by mercy
parts.summary: Believers offer themselves to God, serve one another with their gifts, love their enemies, live under the governing authorities, and welcome one another across disputes about food and days.

parts.title: Paul's plans and greetings
parts.summary: Paul explains his mission, his coming trip to Jerusalem with the collection, and his hope to reach Spain, then greets many believers in Rome by name and closes with praise to God.

parts.title: Greeting and thanksgiving
parts.summary: Paul greets the church as God's holy people and thanks God for its gifts, while pointing ahead to the day of Christ that it must still wait for.

parts.title: Divisions and the wisdom of the cross
parts.summary: Paul answers the reports of factions gathered around leaders. The message of the crucified Christ overturns the world's wisdom and status, and leaders are only servants and stewards of God.

parts.title: Immorality, lawsuits, and the body
parts.summary: Paul confronts a case of incest the church has tolerated, rebukes members for suing one another before pagan courts, and teaches that the body belongs to the Lord and is a temple of the Holy Spirit.

parts.title: Marriage, singleness, and calling
parts.summary: Answering the Corinthians' first question, Paul discusses sexual relations within marriage, divorce, mixed marriages, and the value of remaining single in a time of pressure.

parts.title: Food offered to idols and the use of freedom
parts.summary: Paul addresses eating food sacrificed to idols. Knowledge must give way to love for the weaker brother, Paul gives up his own rights for the gospel, and the church must flee idolatry.

parts.title: Order in worship and the Lord's Supper
parts.summary: Paul addresses head coverings in worship and then rebukes the church for meals where the rich eat while the poor go hungry, handing on the tradition of the Lord's Supper.

parts.title: Spiritual gifts and the way of love
parts.summary: The Spirit gives varied gifts to one body for the common good. Love is the greater way, and worship should be orderly and intelligible so that everyone is built up.

parts.title: The resurrection of the dead
parts.summary: Paul restates the gospel of Christ's death, burial, resurrection, and appearances, argues that the resurrection of believers depends on it, and describes the resurrection body and the final defeat of death.

parts.title: The collection, travel plans, and greetings
parts.summary: Paul gives instructions for the collection for Jerusalem, shares his plans, commends coworkers, and closes with greetings in his own hand.

parts.title: Greeting and the God of all comfort
parts.summary: Paul opens by praising God for comfort in affliction, and tells of a crushing ordeal in Asia from which God delivered him.

parts.title: Changed plans and the tearful letter
parts.summary: Paul defends his integrity in changing his travel plans, explains why he wrote instead of visiting, and urges the church to forgive the offender.

parts.title: The ministry of the new covenant
parts.summary: A long reflection on Paul's ministry: a new covenant of the Spirit, treasure in jars of clay, the hope of the resurrection body, and the message of reconciliation.

parts.title: Titus brings good news
parts.summary: Paul returns to his story: Titus met him in Macedonia with word of the church's repentance, and Paul's anguish turns to joy.

parts.title: The collection for Jerusalem
parts.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to complete their gift for the poor believers in Jerusalem, holding up the Macedonians' generosity and the grace of Christ who became poor.

parts.title: Boasting in weakness against the super-apostles
parts.summary: Paul confronts his rivals, reluctantly boasts as a fool of hardships, visions, and a thorn in the flesh, and prepares the church for his third visit.

parts.title: Greeting and rebuke
parts.summary: Paul greets the churches without a thanksgiving and expresses astonishment that they are turning to a different gospel, which is no gospel at all.

parts.title: Paul's gospel came from Christ
parts.summary: Paul tells how he received his gospel by revelation, how the Jerusalem leaders recognized it, and how he opposed Peter at Antioch. The section ends with a statement of justification by faith in Christ.

parts.title: The argument from Scripture and experience
parts.summary: The Galatians received the Spirit by faith. Abraham was counted righteous by faith, the law came later and could not cancel the promise, and in Christ believers are God's children and Abraham's heirs. Paul appeals to their shared history and to the story of Hagar and Sarah.

parts.title: Freedom and life in the Spirit
parts.summary: Paul warns against circumcision, calls the Galatians to use their freedom to serve one another in love, contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit, and describes how a Spirit-led community treats one another.

parts.title: Closing in Paul's own hand
parts.summary: Paul exposes the agitators' motives, boasts only in the cross, and declares that what counts is a new creation.

parts.title: Greeting and blessing
parts.summary: Paul greets the saints and praises the Father for every spiritual blessing in Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed, forgiven, and sealed with the Spirit.

parts.title: A prayer for understanding
parts.summary: Paul prays that readers will know their hope, their inheritance, and the power that raised Christ and seated him over every rule and authority.

parts.title: Saved by grace, made one
parts.summary: Dead in sin, believers are made alive with Christ by grace through faith; Gentiles once far away are brought near, and Jew and Gentile become one new humanity and one temple.

parts.title: The mystery revealed and a second prayer
parts.summary: Paul explains his calling to make known the mystery that Gentiles are fellow heirs, then prays that readers will grasp the immeasurable love of Christ.

parts.title: Walking worthy of the calling
parts.summary: Keep the unity of the Spirit, use Christ's gifts to build up the body, put off the old self and put on the new, and walk in love, light, and wisdom.

parts.title: The Christian household
parts.summary: Mutual submission shapes the relationships of wives and husbands, children and parents, slaves and masters, all under the one Lord.

parts.title: The armor of God and farewell
parts.summary: Believers stand against the spiritual forces of evil in God's armor and pray; Paul commends Tychicus and closes with peace and grace.

parts.title: Greeting, thanks, and prayer
parts.summary: Paul greets the church, thanks God for their partnership in the gospel, and prays that their love will grow in knowledge and discernment.

parts.title: Paul's circumstances
parts.summary: His imprisonment has advanced the gospel; he rejoices that Christ is preached and weighs life and death, confident he will remain for their sake.

parts.title: A life worthy of the gospel
parts.summary: Stand firm together, look to others' interests, and share the mind of Christ, who emptied himself and was exalted; work out salvation and shine as lights.

parts.title: Timothy and Epaphroditus
parts.summary: Paul plans to send Timothy and sends Epaphroditus home, commending both as examples of self-giving service.

parts.title: Knowing Christ
parts.summary: Paul warns against confidence in the flesh, counts his credentials as loss to gain Christ, presses on toward the goal, and points to citizenship in heaven.

parts.title: Final appeals and thanks
parts.summary: Paul urges unity, joy, prayer instead of anxiety, and right thinking, thanks the church for its gift, and closes with greetings.

parts.title: Greeting, thanks, and prayer
parts.summary: Paul greets the church, thanks God for their faith, love, and hope, and prays that they will be filled with the knowledge of God's will.

parts.title: The supremacy of Christ
parts.summary: The great hymn to Christ as creator and reconciler, followed by its meaning for the Colossians, who have been reconciled if they continue in the faith.

parts.title: Paul's labor for the church
parts.summary: Paul describes his sufferings and his commission to make known the mystery, Christ in you, and his struggle for churches he has never seen.

parts.title: Complete in Christ
parts.summary: Believers are to continue in Christ, in whom the fullness of God dwells, and refuse teaching that binds them to food laws, holy days, visions, and human regulations.

parts.title: The new life
parts.summary: Raised with Christ, believers put off the old self and put on the new, live in love and thankfulness, order their households in the Lord, and pray and speak wisely.

parts.title: Messengers and greetings
parts.summary: Paul commends Tychicus and Onesimus, sends greetings from his coworkers, and closes with a greeting in his own hand.

parts.title: Thanksgiving for the church
parts.summary: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' faith, love, and hope, and for how they welcomed the gospel and turned from idols to serve the living God.

parts.title: Paul's conduct among them
parts.summary: Paul recalls how he and his companions preached with integrity, lived gently among them, and worked night and day, and thanks God that they received the word of God.

parts.title: Paul's longing and Timothy's report
parts.summary: Kept away by force, Paul sent Timothy to strengthen them; Timothy's good news brings him joy, and he prays to see them and for their love to grow.

parts.title: Living to please God
parts.summary: Instruction on sexual holiness, brotherly love, and a quiet life of work that earns the respect of outsiders.

parts.title: The Lord's coming
parts.summary: The dead in Christ will rise and all believers will be with the Lord; the Day of the Lord will come like a thief, so live as children of the day.

parts.title: Life together and farewell
parts.summary: Respect leaders, care for one another, rejoice, pray, give thanks, test prophecy, and receive a closing blessing.

parts.title: Encouragement in persecution
parts.summary: Paul thanks God for the church's growing faith and love under persecution and assures them that God will judge their oppressors and give them relief at the revelation of the Lord Jesus.

parts.title: The Day of the Lord has not come
parts.summary: The rebellion and the man of lawlessness must come first; the lawless one is now restrained, and the Lord Jesus will destroy him at his coming.

parts.title: Chosen and called
parts.summary: Paul thanks God for choosing the Thessalonians for salvation, urges them to stand firm in the traditions they were taught, and prays for their comfort.

parts.title: Request for prayer
parts.summary: Paul asks for prayer for the spread of the word and for deliverance from wicked people, and expresses confidence in the Lord's faithfulness.

parts.title: Warning against idleness and farewell
parts.summary: The church must withdraw from those who refuse to work, following Paul's example, but treat them as brothers, and receive Paul's signed greeting.

parts.title: The charge against false teaching
parts.summary: Paul urges Timothy to stay in Ephesus and stop the false teachers, sets the law in its proper place, and recalls the mercy shown to him, the worst of sinners.

parts.title: Order in God's household
parts.summary: Instructions on prayer for all people, on men and women in worship, and on the character required of overseers and deacons, closing with a confession of the mystery of godliness.

parts.title: False asceticism and a faithful minister
parts.summary: Paul exposes teaching that forbids marriage and foods and urges Timothy to train himself for godliness and give himself to Scripture, teaching, and example.

parts.title: Caring for the whole family
parts.summary: How to treat older and younger members, support true widows, honor and discipline elders, and teach slaves.

parts.title: Godliness, money, and the final charge
parts.summary: False teachers treat religion as a way to profit; Paul warns against the love of money, charges Timothy to fight the good fight, and instructs the rich to be generous.

parts.title: Do not be ashamed
parts.summary: Paul thanks God for Timothy's faith, urges him to fan into flame his gift and share in suffering for the gospel, and contrasts those who deserted him with the loyal Onesiphorus.

parts.title: Be strong and entrust the teaching
parts.summary: Using images of soldier, athlete, farmer, and workman, Paul calls Timothy to endure, remember the risen Christ, handle the word accurately, and correct opponents gently.

parts.title: Hard times and the sufficiency of Scripture
parts.summary: Paul describes the corrupt people of the last days, points to his own example of persecution, and grounds Timothy in the God-breathed Scriptures.

parts.title: Preach the word; the last words of Paul
parts.summary: A solemn charge to preach, Paul's confidence that he has finished his race, and personal requests and greetings as he faces death.

parts.title: Greeting
parts.summary: An unusually full opening in which Paul describes his apostleship in terms of the faith of God's elect and the hope of eternal life.

parts.title: Elders and false teachers
parts.summary: Titus is to appoint elders of proven character who hold to sound teaching, because rebellious teachers must be silenced and rebuked.

parts.title: Teaching for every household
parts.summary: Instructions for older and younger men and women, for Titus himself, and for slaves, grounded in the grace of God that trains believers to live godly lives as they await Christ's appearing.

parts.title: Good citizens saved by mercy
parts.summary: Believers are to be gentle and ready for good works toward all, because God saved them by his mercy through new birth and the Holy Spirit; they must avoid foolish controversies.

parts.title: Travel plans and greetings
