parts.summary: Paul asks Titus to join him at Nicopolis, to help Zenas and Apollos, and to teach believers to meet pressing needs.

parts.title: Greeting
parts.summary: Paul the prisoner and Timothy greet Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church in Philemon's house.

parts.title: Thanksgiving for Philemon's love
parts.summary: Paul thanks God for Philemon's faith and for the love that has refreshed the hearts of the saints, preparing the ground for his request.

parts.title: The appeal for Onesimus
parts.summary: Paul appeals rather than commands, sends Onesimus back as his own heart, asks Philemon to receive him as a beloved brother, and offers to pay whatever he owes.

parts.title: Greetings and blessing
parts.summary: Epaphras, Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke send greetings, and Paul closes with a blessing of grace.

parts.title: The Son, greater than the angels
parts.summary: God has spoken finally in his Son, who is superior to the angels, yet the Son became human, lower than the angels for a while, to suffer, destroy death, and become a merciful high priest. The first warning urges the readers not to drift away.

parts.title: Greater than Moses: entering God's rest
parts.summary: Jesus is faithful as a Son over God's house, as Moses was as a servant in it. Psalm 95 and the wilderness generation warn the church not to harden its heart but to enter the Sabbath rest that still remains.

parts.title: A high priest in the order of Melchizedek
parts.summary: Jesus is a sympathetic high priest, appointed by God. After rebuking the readers' immaturity and warning of falling away, the author assures them of God's oath and shows that Melchizedek's priesthood, eternal and confirmed by oath, surpasses Aaron's.

parts.title: A better covenant, sanctuary, and sacrifice
parts.summary: Christ ministers in the true tabernacle as mediator of the new covenant promised in Jeremiah 31. The Day of Atonement pointed ahead to his single offering of himself, which cleanses the conscience and perfects believers once for all.

parts.title: Draw near and endure by faith
parts.summary: The readers are urged to draw near, hold fast, and meet together, warned against deliberate rejection, and reminded of their earlier courage. The heroes of faith and Jesus himself model endurance, and the unshakable kingdom calls for grateful worship.

parts.title: Life together and farewell
parts.summary: Practical instructions on love, hospitality, marriage, money, and leaders, a call to go to Jesus outside the camp, a benediction, and personal greetings.

parts.title: Trials, wisdom, and the word
parts.summary: James opens with the main themes of the letter: joy and endurance in trials, wisdom asked for in faith, the reversal of rich and poor, the source of temptation, and the call to be doers of the word rather than hearers only.

parts.title: Faith that shows no favoritism and faith that works
parts.summary: Favoring the rich breaks the royal law of love. Faith without deeds is dead, as Abraham and Rahab show.

parts.title: The tongue and the wisdom from above
parts.summary: Teachers face stricter judgment, the tongue is a small fire that can burn a whole life, and true wisdom is known by its peaceable, merciful fruit.

parts.title: Pride, worldliness, and wealth
parts.summary: Quarrels spring from disordered desires. James calls the double-minded to humble themselves before God, rebukes slander and arrogant planning, and pronounces judgment on rich oppressors.

parts.title: Patience, prayer, and restoring the wanderer
parts.summary: Believers wait patiently for the Lord's coming, keep plain speech, pray in every circumstance including sickness, and bring back those who stray.

parts.title: The identity of God's people
parts.summary: After the greeting, Peter praises God for new birth into a living hope, calls the readers to holiness as those redeemed by Christ's blood, and describes them as living stones built into a spiritual house, God's chosen people.

parts.title: Honorable conduct among outsiders
parts.summary: As foreigners and exiles, believers are to live so well that slander fails: submitting to rulers, servants to masters after Christ's example, wives and husbands in mutual honor, and all of them repaying evil with blessing.

parts.title: Suffering for doing good
parts.summary: Peter explains how to suffer for righteousness: with a ready defense of hope, after the pattern of Christ who suffered, died, and was raised. He calls for sober, loving community in the last days and for joy in sharing Christ's sufferings.

parts.title: Elders, humility, and final greetings
parts.summary: Peter exhorts the elders to shepherd willingly, calls all to humility and watchfulness against the devil, promises restoration after suffering, and sends greetings from Babylon.

parts.title: Growing in godliness
parts.summary: After the greeting, Peter reminds readers that God has given them everything for life and godliness, calls them to add virtue to faith, and explains that he writes as a reminder before his death.

parts.title: Eyewitness and prophetic testimony
parts.summary: The apostles did not follow clever myths: they saw Christ's majesty on the holy mountain, and the prophetic word came from God as men were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

parts.title: False teachers and their judgment
parts.summary: False teachers will arise, as false prophets did in Israel. God judged fallen angels, the ancient world, and Sodom while rescuing Noah and Lot, and he will judge these greedy and sensual teachers.

parts.title: The day of the Lord
parts.summary: Scoffers deny Christ's coming, but God's word created and judged the world, God is patient, and the day will come. Believers wait in holiness for a new heaven and earth and grow in grace and knowledge.

parts.title: Prologue: the Word of life
parts.summary: The author and his fellow witnesses proclaim what they heard, saw, and touched, so that readers may share their fellowship with the Father and the Son.

parts.title: Walking in the light
parts.summary: God is light. Walking with him means confessing sin, keeping his commands, loving one's brother, refusing to love the world, and holding to the truth about the Son against the antichrists who have left.

parts.title: Children of God
parts.summary: Those whom the Father has loved and called his children practice righteousness and love one another, as Jesus laid down his life for us.

parts.title: Testing the spirits; God is love
parts.summary: True spirits confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh. God is love, shown in the sending of his Son, and those who know him love one another without fear.

parts.title: Faith, testimony, and assurance
parts.summary: Faith in the Son overcomes the world. God's testimony about his Son gives life, and believers can know they have eternal life, pray with confidence, and keep themselves from idols.

parts.title: Greeting in truth and love
parts.summary: The elder greets the chosen lady and her children, whom he loves in the truth, with grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Son.

parts.title: Walking in truth and love
parts.summary: He rejoices that some of her children walk in the truth and reminds her of the old commandment that we love one another, which means walking in God's commands.

parts.title: Deceivers and the doctrine of Christ
parts.summary: Many deceivers deny Jesus Christ come in the flesh. The church must hold to the teaching of Christ and not welcome or support those who bring another teaching.

parts.title: Closing: hope of a visit
parts.summary: The elder has more to say but hopes to speak face to face, and he sends greetings from the children of the elect sister.

parts.title: Greeting and joy
parts.summary: The elder greets Gaius, wishes him health, and rejoices at reports that he walks in the truth.

parts.title: Hospitality to the brothers
parts.summary: He commends Gaius for welcoming traveling workers who were strangers to him and urges him to send them on in a manner worthy of God.

parts.title: The problem of Diotrephes
parts.summary: Diotrephes, who loves to be first, rejects the elder's authority, slanders him, refuses the brothers, and expels those who would welcome them.

parts.title: Imitate the good; Demetrius commended
parts.summary: Gaius should imitate the good, not the evil. Demetrius has a good testimony from all and from the truth itself.

parts.title: Closing
parts.summary: The elder hopes to visit soon and speak face to face, and sends and asks for greetings among friends.

parts.title: Greeting
parts.summary: Jude, servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, greets those who are called, loved, and kept.

parts.title: Contend for the faith
parts.summary: Jude changes his plan and urges his readers to fight for the faith once delivered, because ungodly people have slipped in, twisting grace and denying Christ.

parts.title: Examples of judgment and portraits of the intruders
parts.summary: Examples from Israel's history and tradition show God's judgment on rebellion, and vivid images describe the intruders, ending with Enoch's prophecy of the Lord's coming.

parts.title: Remember, build, keep, and show mercy
parts.summary: The readers should remember the apostles' warning, build themselves up in faith and prayer, keep themselves in God's love, and show mercy to those who doubt or are in danger.

parts.title: Doxology
parts.summary: Glory to the God who is able to keep believers from stumbling and present them blameless and joyful before him.

parts.title: Prologue and vision of the Son of Man
parts.summary: John introduces the book, greets the seven churches, and sees the risen Christ among seven lampstands, who commissions him to write.

parts.title: Messages to the seven churches
parts.summary: Christ addresses each church in Asia with praise, rebuke, warning, and a promise to the one who overcomes.

parts.title: Throne, scroll, seals, and trumpets
parts.summary: John sees God's throne and the slain Lamb who opens the sealed scroll. Seals and trumpets bring judgments, interludes show the sealed people of God and the faithful witnesses, and the seventh trumpet announces the kingdom.

parts.title: The dragon, the beasts, and the Lamb's people
parts.summary: The conflict behind history is shown: the dragon wars against the woman and her children, the beasts demand worship, and the Lamb stands with his people on Mount Zion.

parts.title: Bowls of wrath and the fall of Babylon
parts.summary: The last plagues are poured out, Babylon the great is judged and mourned, heaven rejoices, and Christ rides out to defeat the beast.

parts.title: The thousand years, judgment, and new creation
parts.summary: Satan is bound, the dead are judged, and John sees the new heaven and new earth and the holy city, where God dwells with his people. The book closes with the promise of Christ's coming.
